item.title: SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL FOR GAO-26-108057: FEMA Assistance for People with Disabilities
item.description:
This is an Easy Read version of GAO's report Disaster Assistance: FEMA Actions Needed to Better Support People with Disabilities in Disasters, GAO-27-108057. Easy Read is a way some groups make their written information easier to understand. For example, Easy Read documents use short sentences and plain language.
In this report, GAO found that the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) gives information to states and communities about helping people with disabilities before, during, and after disasters. FEMA also gives money to help states after a disaster. FEMA used to have training for state and community governments on helping people with disabilities in disasters.FEMA stopped this training in 2025. In some parts of the country, FEMA disability specialists work with states and communities before disasters. But disability specialists' job duties are not always clear.
FEMA gives information about disasters to people with disabilities and their families. It also may give money to people to help them recover after disasters. Some things can make it hard for people with disabilities to apply for disaster money from FEMA. For example, questions on the application may use difficult words without explaining them. FEMA has not asked people with disabilities what they think about the application for disaster money.
GAO made three recommendations in this report to improve help for people with disabilities in disasters.
For more information, contact Elizabeth Curda at curdae@gao.gov.
